label: Brexit referendum
description: The UK votes to leave the EU. Sterling falls roughly 10% on a trade-weighted basis over the following months, feeding through to import prices and pushing CPI from near zero to above 3% by late 2017.

label: COVID-19 lockdown
description: First national lockdown. Bank Rate is cut twice in nine days, from 0.75% to 0.10%. Demand collapses, energy prices fall and CPI drops close to zero — the disinflationary phase that precedes the 2021-22 surge.

label: Hospitality VAT cut to 5%
description: VAT on hospitality and tourism cut from 20% to 5%. It mechanically depresses services CPI, and its staged reversal through 2021-22 mechanically flatters it — a reason to be careful reading services inflation across this window.

label: Reopening & base effects
description: Restrictions lift as the vaccine rollout advances. Base effects against the depressed 2020 price level, plus goods demand meeting constrained supply chains, start pulling headline CPI up from below 1%.

label: European gas price surge
description: Wholesale gas prices spike as post-COVID demand outstrips supply. The Ofgem cap passes this through with a lag, making energy the dominant contributor to headline inflation through 2022.

label: BoE hiking cycle begins
description: The MPC raises Bank Rate from 0.10% to 0.25% — the first hike of the cycle — despite Omicron uncertainty, citing tight labour markets and broadening price pressures.

label: Russia invades Ukraine
description: Energy and food commodity prices spike. For an energy-importing economy this is a terms-of-trade shock: it raises inflation and lowers real incomes simultaneously, which is why the MPC framed it as something to look through only insofar as it did not become persistent.

label: Ofgem cap +54%
description: The domestic energy price cap rises 54% in a single step. Energy alone contributes roughly 2 percentage points to headline CPI over the following months.

label: Mini-Budget
description: Unfunded tax cuts announced without an OBR forecast trigger a gilt sell-off and a sharp fall in sterling. The Bank intervenes in the long-dated gilt market for financial-stability reasons, and market pricing for the terminal Bank Rate briefly moves above 6%.

label: Energy Price Guarantee
description: The EPG caps typical household energy bills, holding energy CPI well below where the Ofgem cap alone would have taken it. It lowers measured headline inflation while supporting demand — an explicit complication for the MPC's reaction function.

label: Headline CPI peaks
description: Headline CPI peaks at 11.1%, a 41-year high. Core and services inflation peak later and fall more slowly — the standard signature of an external shock giving way to domestically generated inflation.

label: Bank Rate peaks at 5.25%
description: The MPC delivers its final hike of the cycle, taking Bank Rate to 5.25%. Headline inflation is falling fast on energy base effects, but services inflation near 7% keeps policy restrictive.

label: CPI returns to 2% target
description: Headline CPI hits the 2% target for the first time since 2021, driven almost entirely by energy base effects. Services inflation remains close to 6%, which is why the MPC did not cut at this meeting.

label: First cut of the easing cycle
description: The MPC cuts Bank Rate to 5.00% on a 5-4 vote, describing the move as a removal of some restrictiveness rather than the start of a rapid easing cycle.

label: Employer NICs rise
description: The increase in employer National Insurance contributions and the National Living Wage raises labour costs for services-intensive sectors, a channel the MPC watched closely for pass-through into services prices.
